geopolitics_summary: COP31 negotiating immediate fossil-fuel transition language; EU climate ambitions wavering on electrification; Russia Arctic LNG reroute to Asia from 2027 reduces EU supply pressure.

themes.headline: EU may soften clean power electrification push at COP31
themes.why_it_matters: Weakened electrification targets reduce long-term structural demand for EU power; delays coal/gas phase-out assumptions underlying forward curve risk premiums.

themes.headline: Russia reroutes Arctic LNG to Asia; Europe no longer buying from 2027
themes.why_it_matters: Elimination of Russian LNG supply narrows EU gas import sources; tightens TTF curve, raises LNG swing supply reliance on Atlantic basin and re-export routes; supports power baseload costs.

themes.headline: COP31 draft text signals immediate fossil fuel transition commitment
themes.why_it_matters: Strengthened global climate commitments increase EUA risk premium via tighter EU ETS Phase 2 outlook; supports coal displacement and power fuel-switch margin compression.

themes.headline: Southwest US hydropower generation hits record lows in 2026 summer
themes.why_it_matters: Drought-driven US hydro collapse reduces Henry Hub pressure from marginal gas burn; indirect upside to US LNG export margins, constraining available Atlantic swing supply to EU TTF.

themes.headline: COP31 negotiators target methane super-pollutant reduction agreement
themes.why_it_matters: Methane reduction commitments may tighten supply-side compliance for gas producers; supports carbon costs and fuel-switching economics in power generation.
